For example, inside method one, I may update the data like method inside the Threadlocal, but the other method that we are invoking from the same thread, it may update the value to some other name like John.

So this will be a problem, because any method that is being executed by the thread can mutate the data that we stored inside the threadlocal. To debug any runtime issues or defects around these threadlocal, it is going to be a lot of work to the developers because they clearly can't track which method update to what value, and this will result into some unexpected results as well. The next problem is around the unbounded lifetime. As I said before, when these threadlocal is being used, once the data is set and once the data is retrieved by using the set and get methods, and once the developer feels like he is done with the thread context data, the developer has to make sure to invoke the remove method.

But in reality, most of the developers, they are not invoking this remove method, even in the enterprise applications as well. And with that, what is going to happen? The data is going to store forever inside that thread, inside Java and inside frameworks like spring, there is a concept called thread pool. So as part of this thread pool, what the developer or what the framework is going to do is they're going to create a good amount of threads like maybe 50 or 100, and they are going to maintain all these threads into the pool.

Since the creation of a thread is a time consuming operation, usually during the startup, the framework are the developers, they're going to create a required amount of threads like 50 and 100, and they are going to maintain inside a pool. So whenever a request comes, the thread will be retrieved from this pool and will be assigned to the request handling. And let's imagine as part of a request handling, I stored some data into a thread with the user information and once the request is done with these request to processing, the same thread will go back to the thread pool.

Next time when another request comes, the same thread will be assigned to the new request. And if the new request also is setting some some other data or some other information inside the thread local. So this way the same thread will end up storing a good amount of data because we are never shutting down the thread, or we are never killing the thread from processing the request. The shutting down of the threads inside the thread pool will only happen when the application is getting restarted, or when it is getting shut down.

So with the thread pool concept, the thread is going to have unbounded lifetime. And if the developer forgets to invoke the remove method, all the data that we are trying to store inside the thread locals, they are going to be increased exponentially and at some point of time we are going to have memory footprint issues or memory leak issues as well. So what is a memory leak? Let's imagine a request to one is processed by thread one, and as part of this request one, I stored some data like modern using the thread local.

If I don't invoke the remove method and the request is processed, the thread will go back to the thread pool and for the request two if the same thread is assigned. So this request will have the information around the modern because this information is still hang to this thread t1. Due to this, what is happening? The memory is getting leaked from one request to other request and this may result into security vulnerabilities, memory issues and performance issues.

The third problem that we have with the thread local is expensive inheritance. When we are creating a thread, we can also create it. A child threads by using the inheritance concept. So I can create a child thread. So if this is a parent thread, the child thread, it is going to inherit all the data that we store inside this parent thread by using the thread local concept. If I end up multiple channels and subchannels of a thread at some point of time, the most recent child thread, it will end up storing all the memory that we stored inside the parent and super parent threads.

Using this thread local that will result into memory overhead, especially with the virtual threads. So virtual threads is a new concept which is introduced in Java 21. We know virtual threads are lightweight threads, so from a single platform thread we can create millions of virtual threads. And if all these millions of virtual threads inherit the data from the same platform thread, it will leads into memory overhead. That's why to resolve all these problems, especially since nowadays the developers are inclined to use the virtual threads in new modern approach is introduced with the name scope to value.

With the scope to values. We are going to overcome all the disadvantages of thread local. Let's continue this discussion in the next lecture as well.
